title: Rate Premium on Delayed Lienholder Releases
content:
## Rate premium on delayed lienholder releases — Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda

A refund released to the lienholder under the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda carries a rate premium that grows with the time between the effective date of the cancellation (the waiver's closing date) and the release date. The premium is added to the yearly rate at which the late-release interest runs, and the interest is then figured on that combined rate.

| Release made, counted in calendar days after the effective date | Premium added to the yearly interest rate |
|---|---|
| More than 60 days | 0.02 (2 percentage points) |
| 31 to 60 days | 0.01 (1 percentage point) |
| Within 30 days | Nothing |

### Band edges

- Day 30 after the effective date: no premium. Day 31: 0.01.
- Day 60: 0.01. Day 61: 0.02.
- The effective date itself is day 0.

### Basis questions

**Which date starts the count?** The effective date of the cancellation, which is the waiver's closing date, or the release date where the waiver carries none.

**Is the premium a fixed amount?** No. It is a yearly rate added to the interest rate, so its money effect depends on the refund due and the late days.

### Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A refund due of 655.10 is released on day 45 after the effective date, with 21 late days and an interest rate of 0.05. The premium is 0.01, so the interest runs at 0.06: 655.10 times 0.06 times 21, divided by 365, is 2.261…, rounded half up to 2.26.
